Harbor lanterns return to Pier 4

By Mina Cole · 12 March 2024

The city restored 40 copper lanterns along Pier 4 this week, ending a two-year gap after salt corrosion took the originals out of service. Officials said the replicas follow the 1912 pattern but use sealed LED modules so crews can replace bulbs without climbing the posts.

Night ferry operators argued the dark stretch made boarding slower in winter fog. A harbor survey recorded 18 near-misses at the pier since 2022, though none caused injuries. The transportation bureau did not release the raw incident log with the announcement.

Neighbors are split. Some welcome the warmer light; others worry the LEDs will spill into apartment windows. The bureau promised a dimming schedule after midnight but did not publish the lux targets.
